January 2010 # New Year uncertainty and volatility - After the upheaval of the global financial crisis, copper prices bounced back rapidly fuelled by an active Chinese market through much of 2009. However in the absence of any marked recovery in the world ex-Asia, global exchange stocks have slowly begun to accumulate, as Chinese buying slows. - The degree (or absence) of a recovery in the world economy will determine demand prospects for copper. China and the rest of Asia will be unable to support the market without some follow through from the muted European and American economies. But Nexans and Prysmian are doubtful of a wire and cable demand recovery in 2010. - Prices are likely to be volatile as we head into the New Year, not least given the possibility of further strikes in Chile and Africa and dollar movement. Rebalancing of commodity indices in early January will only compound short-term volatility. |The supply/demand

# Stalling Copper’s rally and the associated volatility have diminished since our last Monitor with prices failing to build on the increases in November. Although the 3-month price hit a fresh 2009 high of around $7,160/t in early December, a combination of rising exchange inventories (up 35,000t since the end of November) and a stronger dollar have remained key sources of downward pressure, capping prices at around the $7,000/t level. Prices have traded well above $6,000/t since the middle of the year and as we look ahead into 2010 are unlikely to fall below this level in the coming quarter. The market is much healthier now than it was at **2800** the end of 2008, supported by positive economic **Jan-09 Mar-09 May-09 Jul-09 Aug-09 Oct-09** data, which all indicate that the worst of the global Data: LME economic crisis is over. That said the Dubai debt drama that came to light late in November has been a timely reminder of the fragility of the global financial system. It highlights a protracted recovery that will be delicate but subject to periodic shocks that will undoubtedly rattle confidence. China and the countries of Asia (excluding Japan) are spearheading the economic recovery, while the USA, Europe and Japan remain laggards. All indications point to patchy improvement in these developed economies, with German factory orders down for the first time in eight months in October while a survey of purchasing managers showed that European service and manufacturing industries expanded at their fastest pace in more than two years in December, with the PMI increasing to 54.2 from 53.7 in November. ## **Cautious optimism** It comes as no surprise therefore that US and European consumers are taking a cautious tone over their commitments for 2010. Negotiations for the annual copper contracts are still under discussion in these regions and are likely to be drawn out, with volumes conservative, but certainly up on 2009 levels. What is clear is that the cathode consumers in Europe and the USA are not anticipating a rebound in demand from their end-use sectors. Their markets have finally stabilised at a low level and any overall real pick up in demand will depend on developments in the global economy. On a positive note, and unlike the situation a year ago, consumers are now carrying very low levels of inventory as they head into 2010 especially given the absence of any clarity in their downstream product pipe line and high copper prices. If business perks up unexpectedly in January, this could result in a flurry of activity and those consumers that are not adequately covered by long term commitments would be left open to the vagaries of the spot market. In contrast negotiations in Asia have progressed well, with the Chinese keen to lock in annual contracts at terms of $85/t. On balance the spot market has been fairly qu

iet ahead of the year-end hiatus. In Europe spot premiums have been supported in a $50-70/t range on a CIF Rotterdam basis and with warrants tightly held there is no incentive to offer any discount for prompt delivery. The spot premium in China for imported copper cathodes has edged higher since last month to $60-70/t, supported by the higher annual premiums and the narrowing Shanghai/LME arbitrage (implying that the imports should theoretically flow into China). © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 2 of 12 Copper Monitor January 2010 www.crumonitor.com Given the volume of material that has been imported so far this year, we would be surprised if the latest contraction in the arbitrage will trigger any substantial buying. Premiums in the USA are in a broad range of 3.5-4.5¢/lb, but with scrap flowing freely and business very soft in the approach to the year end, physical business has been limited. Recent Chilean tenders also confirm the softer tone (see table at the bottom of page 5). ## **A two speed recovery** As we alluded to earlier, Asia is not only holding the banner for economic growth but for copper demand as well. Taiwan offers a snapshot of developments elsewhere in the region. The domestic economy is clearly improving with construction activity and electricity generation showing sustained sequential improvement from the depths of January 2009. Taiwanese cable shipments dropped to recessionary lows in January 2009 ( _see chart on the right_ ) as producers, distributors and consumers destocked in the face of financial turmoil, cancelled orders and collapsing copper prices. However there was an unexpectedly brisk sequential recovery in Q1 and an upturn in domestic and export orders followed. This momentum was related to the even stronger recovery in cable demand in Mainland China, giving Taiwanese cablemakers Taiwanese metallic cable

the confidence that the economic improvement would inevitably spread to the Taiwanese economy. September seems to have been a more decisive step on the road to recovery with shipments jumping 13.2% m-o-m and just 5.2% below year-ago levels. Encouragingly, the improvement is broad based with domestic shipments only 5.8% down y-o-y and export sales down by only 3.4% y-o-y. Metallic cable production has recovered a little faster, posting a 1.5% rise, the first y-o-y increase for 12 months, as manufacturers’ inventories have normalised, suggesting that the recovery is more or less complete through the supply chain. CRU expects that the release of subsequent cable shipment data f

or metallic cables for the rest of 2009 will show sizeable y-o-y gains against the weakest months of 2008. However that will not be enough to reverse the cumulative damage inflicted in the first nine months. But if the Asian economic recovery continues then there are strong hopes that the Taiwanese cable industry should be able to achieve further gains in early-2010. Despite the signs of recovery in copper demand in Asia, the market in North America and Europe have not yet improved, and therefore we remain cautious about an early consumption recovery within these critical regions. The US rod sector is a case in point. Underlying activity in the power and construction sectors is still depressed with no sign that these sectors will pick up any time soon. This is reflected in the latest domestic shipment data which saw levels in October 17% below year-ago results. Preliminary data show a further double digit decline in November shipments, down 18.8% y-o-y with year-to-date shipments down 24% in the first 11months. The continued steep y-o-y decline in November is significant because November 2008 was a very weak month. ## **IPO fever** Last months Copper Monitor highlighted the growing risk appetite of investors buoyed by rising equity and commodity prices, including copper. This appetite for risk was borne out both by an increased © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 3 of 12 Copper Monitor January 2010 www.crumonitor.com number of copper mine asset purchases and a growing number of mine company IPOs, particularly on the Australian Stock Exchange (ASX). The question we asked at that time was - is this flow of money into commodities, including copper, going to be sustained? The rush to raise capital while

Since then we have seen a further significant copper mine acquisition, with the Japanese trading house, Sojitz, purchasing a 25% share in the Gibraltar **15** copper mine in Canada for around C$180M. It is however on the stock exchanges where most of the activity has been. Using the ASX as an example, **10** November saw three mining IPOs, following four in October and three in September. This contrasts with **5** the year to August total of only five. So far, December has seen twelve mining IPOs and the ASX is indicating that at least another ten more are **0** planned. This number is over twice the number of **2008J** IPO’s per month than the halcyon days of June and July 2008, which marked the top of the commodities bubble. For many spectators this number of IPOs looks something akin to a run on a bank, where if you do not get to the bank before th

e money runs out, you end up with nothing. Australian junior mine executives and underwriters clearly fear that equity finance will dry up next year, and that it is best to raise capital now. Of the ten planned IPOs before the end of the year, two of the largest have already been delayed, one being the Q Copper listing, who hoped to restart CopperCo’s Lady Annie mine in Australia. All this is indicative of an equity bubble, which therefore does not bode well for equity markets in Q1 2010. Furthermore, as we saw at the end of 2008 commodity prices do tend to follow equity prices down. A sudden lack of equity finance will only make raising money more difficult for smaller mining companies. With a dearth of large projects due on stream in 2010 this will further restrict supply, supporting prices and exacerbating an extremely tight concentrates market. Stocks of concentrate are reportedly extremely low and with mine output expected to register limited growth in 2010, the latest round of TC/RC negotiations will be difficult. Contract TC/RCs will be lower than the terms agreed last year reflecting the excess of smelting and refining capacity relative to concentrate supply alongside lower sulphuric acid prices. Smelters will need higher TC/RCs to survive, particularly in the face of lower sulphuric acid prices and increasing operating and capital costs. Current indications are that contract TC/RCs wil settle around or below the $50/5¢ level. There are rumours of a settlement at $43/4.3¢, but this is not believed to be one of the benchmark contracts. ### **2010 – a year of recovery** The outlook for 2010 will be heavily dependent on developments at a global level. The performance of the US dollar will be a determining and important component as will the Chinese requirement of cathode, the impact of which we have seen this past year. If China does not emerge once again as the buyer of last resort and lure copper off the market, it is likely that surpluses will become visible in the form of rapidly rising exchange inventories and limit further prices rallies. The primary end-market for copper plumbing tube is the construction sector. Copper commercial tube is used in the fabrication of air conditioners and refrigerators whilst copper alloy tube is consumed in industrial machinery and equipment. Our estimates show that world consumption of copper and alloy tube will fall by 12.5% y-o-y to 2.6M tonnes in 2009. The most severe decline was experienced in copper plumbing tube, which will contract by 17.9% to 0.6M tonnes. This is a result of the slowdown encountered in the residential and commercial construction sectors. In fact, 2009 is the fifth consecutive year that world consumption of copper plumbing tube will decline. The world market of copper commercial tube is anticipated to have shrunk by 10.4% to 1.5M tonnes in 2009, following a 2.2% drop in 2008. The HVACR market was impacted by the slowdown in construction activity and the decline in private spending. Our figures show that the US market in 2009 will be down by 26.5% y-o-y to 170,000 tonnes. China, the world’s largest market, will drop by 2.4% to 653,000 tonnes. World copper alloy tube sales will decrease by 11.1% to 0.5M tonnes in 2009. It was the only segment that saw growth in 2008, supported by demand from the industrial sector and heavy infrastructure projects in developing regions. ## **Production responded to ailing demand** Production of copper plumping tube in Western Europe is estimated to have fallen by 20.9% to 224,000 tonnes in 2009. We anticipate that German production of copper plumbing tube will plunge by 21.9% to 67,000 tonnes in 2009. US output will fall to 132,000 tonnes in 2009, down by 23.5% from 2008. In copper commercial tube, China has emerged as the most aggressively expanding national producer with a significant amount of installed capacity. Chinese output in 2009 will total an estimated 748,000 tonnes, which is still 5% down compared with the previous year. Our figures show that the Indian Subcontinent also is exhibiting a gradual long-term increase in production. Western European output of copp

er commercial tube is expected to have plummeted by 26.3% to 138,000 tonnes, after the major regional fabricators adjusted their production levels. US output will fall to 152,000 tonnes in 2009 down from 240,000 tonnes in 2005. Due to the slowdown in industrial activity, we estimate that copper alloy tube production in Western Europe will contract by 25.2% to 83,000 tonnes in 2009. Germany and Italy suffered significantly from falling demand for industrial equipment. In North East Asia, Japan follows a similar pattern, however South Korea is expected to exhibit growth of 15% to 23,000 tonnes in 2009. ## **Copper substitution pressures stronger than ever** The copper commercial tube and copper plumbing tube segments are particularly vulnerable to substitution threats from competing materials. Now that the copper:aluminium price ratio has reached all time high levels, copper commercial tube consumers are considering aluminium as an alternative solution. © 2009 CRU International Ltd **confidential** Page 8 of 12 Copper Monitor January 2010 www.crumonitor.com In addition, with the copper price hovering around $7,000/t, copper plumbing tube has become once again less attractive when compared to plastic and composite tube products that are continuously gaining market share supported by a number of competitive advantages and marketing campaigns. As a result, along with the market shrinkage, the copper plumbing tube and copper commercial tube segments are seriously challenged by substitution pressures that make copper a less competitive material. ##### **Copper Tube and Pipe Service 2009** The Tube and Pipe report provides detailed analysis and five year forecasts of this complicated market, covering copper plumping tube, copper commercial tube and copper alloy tube. The report provides consumption analysis by region and end-use market. Production is segmented by region and company, with rankings and shares. In addition, the major regional trends in trade are reviewed; this volume features a brief study of the US copper tube imports too. Five-year detailed forecast figures are included as well. This new report is part of CRU’s highly respected Copper and Wire & Cable Team’s unrivalled Copper Semis Service, which provides analysis and five year forecasts of the major refined copper consuming sectors – Flat Rolled, Tube and Pipe, Rod, Bar and Wire and Wirerod. ed workers at **Codelco's Chuquicamata** mine blocked access roads for 19 hours after labour contract negotiations broke down.  The current three year contract is set to expire on December 31<sup>st</sup> , but talks between the state-owned miner and union leaders to agree a new contract have been abandoned, with some reports indicating that the unions were unhappy with Codelco's proposal to exchange a number of contractual benefits for higher pay.  Workers had asked for a 7.5% salary increase in their new 30-month collective labour contract.   Chuquicamata had been expected to produce around 358,000 tonnes of copper-in-concentrate and 150,000t of EW cathode in 2009. 

- In late November, the management and the union at **Antamina** in Peru (jointly owned by **BHP Billiton** , **Xstrata** , **Teck** and **Mitsubishi Corporation** ) agreed a new collective labour contract after four months of negotiations.  The new contract will last three years.  In 2009, CRU expects that Antamina will produce 338,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

- It was reported that operations at **Luanshya Copper Mines** ( **LCM** )’s **Baluba** mine (Zambia) resumed on 15<sup>th</sup> December, two weeks ahead of schedule, after the modernisation of the copper processing plant.  LCM, majority owned by **China Non** - **Ferrous Mining Corporation** (CNMC), spent $70M on the project.  In 2008, Baluba produced 20,000t of copper-in-concentrates and was placed on care and maintenance in December 2008. 

- On 26<sup>th</sup> November, **Inmet Mining** announced that the National Executive Council of the Government of Papua New Guinea has given its consent to the exchange of Inmet's 18% equity interest in **Ok Tedi Mining Limited** (OTML) for a 5% net smelter return (NSR) royalty on revenues of product from the Ok Tedi mine.  Only gains and losses from hedging and forward sales in effect as of 18<sup>th</sup> May 2009 would be considered to determine proceeds under the NSR.  The NSR is expected to continue from closing of the deal to 31<sup>st</sup> December 2013.  On that date Inmet Mining will receive 18% of OTML’s working capital as of the effective date and will cease to be shareholder of OTML (including rights and obligations).  In 2009, CRU expects Ok Tedi to produce 161,000t of copper-inconcentrate. 

- **PT Freeport Indonesia** announced on 16th December that it is in talks with the West Papuan regional government about selling a portion of **Freeport McMoRan Copper & Gold** ’s 90.64% stake in the company to the local government. The potential size of the stake has not been revealed. PT Freeport Indonesia operates the **Grasberg** copper-gold mine in West Papua, and in 2009 CRU expects Grasberg to produce 752,000t of copper-in-concentrate. 

## **Exploration and Development** 



- On 1<sup>st</sup> December, **Zijin Mining Group** started a friendly takeover bid for **Indophil Resources** – including **Xstrata Copper’s** 19.9% stake – for A$545M.  Xstrata Copper agreed tha

t they will sell each share at A$1.28 (equivalent to $498M for the whole stake), subject to certain conditions. Indophil Resources’ main asset is a 32.23% stake in the **Tampakan** copper–gold project in the Philippines.  In addition, Zijin is also accelerating the acquisition of **Alsons Corporation’s** 3.27%

- stake in Tampakan.  CRU expects the Tampakan project to possibly start production by 2016 and reach 330,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate when operating at full capacity. 









- On 10<sup>th</sup> December, **Kazakhmys** announced a US$5B investment programme.  The plan allocates US$1B for refining facilities within the next five years and a further US$4B to build two large blocks at **Boschekul** and **Aktogay** copper deposits that would allow the company to increase their processing capacity by 30%.  In 2009, CRU expects Kazakhmys to produce 353,000t of copper-inconcentrates. 

- **Xstrata** announced a $542M investment to extend the life of **Ernest Henry** , its copper–gold mine in Queensland, Australia.  The investment will allow the mine to shift from open pit to underground and remain operating until at least 2024.  Construction of the extension is expected to start in 2010, with production beginning in late 2011.  From 2012, Xstrata expects the production level at Ernest Henry to be 50,000t/y of copper-in-concentrate.  Concentrates from the mine will continue go to Xstrata's nearby Mount Isa smelter, and the anode to its Townsville refinery.  In 2009, CRU expects Ernest Henry to produce 74,000t of copper-in-concentrates. 

- On 11<sup>th</sup> December, the **International Monetary Fund** (IMF) approved a loan of US$551M to the **DR Congo** to support their poverty reduction and growth strategy.  The loan will help achieve debt relief and mobilize additional donor assistance, amongst other benefits.  The DR Congo and **China** had previously agreed an infrastructure-for-minerals agreement, but the IMF argued that this would increase the DR Congo’s external debt.  In addition, the infrastructure-for-minerals agreement was cut from US$9B to US$6B in August 2009. 

- On December 7<sup>th</sup> it was announced that **Pan Pacific Copper** have begun a feasibility study for the **Quechua** copper deposit in Peru's Cuzco region. If the project goes ahead, the company plans to commission it as early as August 2014, and the operation is projected to produce an average of 76,000 t/y of copper-in-concentrate during its 17-year mine life. 

## **Smelting and Refining** 









- On 8<sup>th</sup> December, **Xstrata Copper** announced that it will permanently cease operation of its copper and zinc facilities at the **Kidd Metallurgical** site in Timmins, Ontario, Canada on 1<sup>st</sup> May 2010.  The Kidd mine and concentrator will remain in operation.  In 2009, CRU expects Kidd to produce 68,000t of copper blister.

- It was reported that **Chinese** and **Japanese** smelters have increase their expectations for **TC/RCs** to around US$60/6¢ (from US$50/5¢), following Xstrata’s announcement about their Kidd plant closure.  BHP Billiton has offered TC/RCs of US$43/4.3¢.  Contracts for 2009 with Chinese smelters had TC/RCs of US$75/7.5¢. 

- It was reported that **Hindustan Copper** plans to outsource the processing of 55,000t of copper-inconcentrated into copper cathodes.  The decision aims to maintain the company’s share in the refined copper market.  The tenders are expected on the 16<sup>th</sup> December.  In December 2008, Hindustan closed their 31,000t-capacity **Khetri** smelter.  In 2009, CRU expects Hindustan Copper to produce 16,000t of refined copper. 

- The **Chinese government** has removed Value Added Tax (VAT) charges levied on gold contained in imported blister copper as of 1<sup>st</sup> November 2009.  VAT on gold contained in copper concentrates had

## **Consumption** 









- Japanese wire and cable manufacturer **Furukawa Electric** announced plans to build new wiring harness plants in Brazil, India and China over the next 3 years.  This move is part of its strategy to acquire majority stakes in its joint venture production sites around the world.  The company is expecting sales in China to reach RMB32-35B (US$5B) in 2013, with a new harness plant planned for Wuhan adding to its five existing auto parts plants in the country. 

- **Ducab** is planning a US$136M joint venture cable project with **Dubai’s Water and Electricity Authority (DEWA)** and **Abu Dhabi’s Water and Electricity Authority (ADWEA)** to help expand public sector electricity networks.  The project is located in the Jebel Ali area.  Production is expected to start in 12 months and will supply DEWA and ADWEA with high voltage cables.  A third of its output will be exported to the Gulf States. 

- **Nexans** , the world’s largest wire and cable manufacturer, said that it saw no immediate upturn in demand for cables next year given that the market has stabilised at a very low level.  However, a boom in wind farm and power network projects is providing some relief for the group’s sales. Meanwhile, the group announced its largest ever wind power contract, a €100M (US$145M) deal for submarine power cables for the London Array off-shore project. 

- **Jiangxi Mingxin Copper Industry** said it has started a copper fabricating project in Yingtai Industry Park.  The project will be completed in February 2011 and is expected to generate revenue of RMB1B (US$147M) and pre-tax profits of RMB41M (US$6M).  It has also been reported that Fujian merchants have invested RMB360M (US$53M) in the project.
